bio_en: Malkhas (Artashes Hovsepian) was born in Trabzon on the night of 24 February 1877 and studied there under Simon Zavarian and then at the Sanasarian school in Erzurum, which he left to devote himself to revolutionary work. In 1896, before the Hamidian massacres, he went to America, where he became a party worker and contributor to Hairenik, publishing his first novel in 1902 under the name Mir-Hazor. Invited by Zavarian to Geneva in 1903, he met Kristapor and Rostom, then went to Tiflis and took part in the Yerevan demonstrations over the church properties; in 1907 he entered Van in disguise, and was later held for four months in Metekh prison. He died in Beirut on 4 January and received a national funeral there.
